messages:
sanjay: Heads up — high-priority customer escalation. They see duplicate billing events when our Python SDK retries after 429/503. We have a repro and partial logs, need SDK team help asap.

maya: Thanks, Sanjay. Can you paste the minimal repro and the SDK version? Also the API request_id/correlation if you have it.

sanjay: Repro steps below. SDK: redwood-python 0.11.2 (customer pinned). On our side we see two successful POSTs to /v1/charges with different server timestamps but same payload. Server logs show the first returned 503 then a 200, but the SDK retried and we got duplicate charge.

sanjay: Repro (sanitized):
```
# pip install redwood==0.11.2
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="sk-REDACTED")
resp = client.charges.create(amount=1000, currency="usd", idempotency_key=None)
print(resp)
```
We deliberately did not set idempotency_key; customer relied on SDK to attach it.

eli: Hmm — SDK should generate an idempotency key by default for mutating endpoints. If it didn't, that's already a problem. Any X-Request-ID / x-redwood-request in the logs?

sanjay: Server logs: request_id=01G7QZ2X-SRV; sequence:
```
[12:03:01.123] POST /v1/charges -> 503 (timeout) request_id=01G7QZ2X-SRV
[12:03:01.654] POST /v1/charges -> 200 (created) request_id=01G7QZ2X-SRV
```
Client logs (SDK debug) show a retry 100ms later which also POSTed and returned 200 with request_id=01G7QZ2X-SRV. So server shows two 200s.

alex: Do we have correlation to SDK-side idempotency header? The header we expect is Idempotency-Key.

support-bot: Attached customer metadata: account=acct_72, region=us-west-2, timeframe=2026-03-10T12:03:00Z.

maya: Sanjay — can you check the raw request headers that hit our edge from the SDK? If the SDK generated a key it should be present. If the SDK omitted it on retry then there was a bug.

sanjay: Raw headers from edge (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/charges
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: redwood-python/0.11.2
Idempotency-Key:  -- MISSING --
X-Redwood-Request: 01G7QZ2X-SRV
```
The retry attempt also lacked Idempotency-Key.

eli: Ok that's the smoking gun — 0.11.2 seems not to attach idempotency on retries. I recall a patch in 0.11.4 that changed retry flow to preserve generated idempotency_key across attempts. Can you confirm customer tested 0.11.4?

sanjay: Customer upgraded to 0.11.4 in a staging run and duplicate billing stopped. They can reproduce on 0.11.2 consistently.

eli: Two separate issues likely: (1) idempotency_key generation/persistence bug in 0.11.2, (2) jitter/backoff anomaly that makes retries happen too soon. Any evidence of backoff values?

maya: Customer logs include timestamps between attempts ~100-200ms, which is lower than expected for exponential with jitter. Could be deterministic jitter bug (jitter=0 or negative).

alex: Eli, can you check changelog around retry code and jitter implementation? Might be a bad port of the JS logic.

eli: Will do. Quick notes: code snippet from 0.11.2 retry loop (excerpt):
```
# pseudo
for attempt in range(max_attempts):
    response = _request()
    if should_retry(response):
        delay = base * (2 ** attempt) * random.uniform(0, 1)  # intended jitter
        time.sleep(delay)
        continue
    return response
```
I suspect random.uniform(0,1) was accidentally replaced with random.choice([0]) in a build step for determinism in tests, and that ended up released. Also idempotency_key generation may have been inside the retry loop so regenerated each attempt.

eng-bot: Deploy note: unit test change 0.11.3-ci pinned random for deterministic tests.

maya: Workarounds for customers now?

eli: Short-term: advise pinning to 0.11.4 or set explicit Idempotency-Key per request. Also set retry.max_attempts=1 to avoid retries until patch is out. For billing refunds we should proactively reverse duplicate charges and notify customer.

sanjay: Doing refunds now and told customer to upgrade. They're asking for root cause and whether we will issue a security/bug disclosure.

eli: Root cause summary (draft): in redwood-python 0.11.2 a test-helper change accidentally made jitter deterministic and idempotency key generation occur inside the retry loop causing new keys per attempt. This combination can lead to duplicate server-side effects when the first attempt times out but succeeds server-side. Patch in 0.11.4 moves idempotency generation outside the loop and restores non-deterministic jitter.

maya: I'll escalate to account team with mitigation steps and ETA for formal write-up.

alex: Filing SDK incident ticket ENG-RT-832 and assigning to @eli. Please link to reproducer and logs.

eli: Got it. I'll prepare PR with unit tests and coordinate a point release. Also adding integration test to assert Idempotency-Key is identical across retries and backoff is non-zero.

sanjay: Thanks all. I'll update the customer and include timelines. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Note: this thread recorded an action item: refund processed for acct_72, sdk_patch_required=true.
